scenes.heading: Interdependence in ecosystems
scenes.say: No organism lives alone. Every species depends on others for food, shelter or pollination. So why can removing just one species change a whole ecosystem?

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Close a major train interchange and trips all over the city stop
scenes.science: Lose a keystone species and the whole food web changes
scenes.breaks: Trains run both ways, but energy in a food web flows one way: from the eaten to the eater.
scenes.say: Think of a food web like a city's train network. Each species is a station, and each feeding link is a line. Close a major interchange, and trips all over the city are disrupted. That's like losing a keystone species. But energy only flows one way in a food web: arrows point to the mouth.

scenes.heading: Predator–prey cycles
points: Predator peaks lag behind prey peaks
scenes.say: Predator and prey populations often rise and fall in linked cycles. Plenty of prey means more predators. More predators means fewer prey. Then predators starve and fall, and prey recover. Predator peaks come a little after prey peaks, because extra food takes time to become extra offspring.

scenes.heading: Symbiosis by score
scenes.say: Symbiosis is a close, long-term relationship between two species. In mutualism, both benefit, like coral and its zooxanthellae. In commensalism, one benefits and the other is unaffected, like an orchid on a tree. In parasitism, the parasite gains and the host is harmed, like mistletoe on a eucalypt.

scenes.heading: Types of competition

right.title: Interspecific
points: Rabbits vs native herbivores for grass

scenes.say: Competition is lose-lose: both get less of the resource. Intra means within one species. Inter means between different species. Species can avoid it by resource partitioning, like feeding at different heights or times.

scenes.heading: Remove a keystone species
scenes.question: Dingoes are removed from an area. Predict two effects on the ecosystem.
lines: Foxes and cats may become more common
→ more predation on small native mammals
scenes.say: Dingoes are widely seen as a keystone predator in parts of Australia. What if they're removed? Kangaroo numbers may rise, leading to overgrazing. Foxes and cats may become more common, increasing predation on small native mammals. One species affects many others.

Quick recap. Food web arrows point to the mouth. Predator peaks lag behind prey peaks. Learn the symbiosis scores. And keystone species, like dingoes, have effects far bigger than their numbers. Now try the practice questions!
